previous_statement: Differentiating the exact quadratic equation gives ||DG(T)||<=(1+epsilon_r)||Z_T||*(1+||DG(T)||). For ||T||<=2r, ||Z_T||<=(1+d)||T||<=3r. Hence a universal cutoff epsilon_r+r<=b_g makes 3(1+epsilon_r)r<=1/2, allows absorption, and yields ||DG(T)||<=K_g*r for a universal K_g depending only on the fixed C_g,k_g.
new_statement: For every T in B_{2delta}^{icalH}(0) with ||T||<=2r, differentiating the exact quadratic equation in an arbitrary icalH-direction gives ||DG(T)||<=(1+epsilon_r)||Z_T||*(1+||DG(T)||). Node 1.3.1 gives ||Z_T||<=(1+d)||T||<=3r because d<=1/2. Thus, if epsilon_r+r<=b_g:=1/7, then a:=3(1+epsilon_r)r<=24/49<1/2; hence ||DG(T)||<=a/(1-a)<=6(1+epsilon_r)r<=7r. Therefore ||DG(T)||<=K_g*r on this domain with the universal choice K_g=7 (and in particular K_g depends only on the fixed provider data).
